segments.text: Scientists are using thunderquakes to
see what's hidden underground. Cuz when
lightning strikes, it heats up the air
around it and creates a shockwave that
you hear as thunder. And when that
energy hits the ground, it also creates
seismic ripples in the dirt and rock.
That's a thunderquake. These
thunderquakes can penetrate deep into
the ground. And to listen to them,
scientists used buried internet cables
that are full of tiny glass fibers
carrying data in the form of light.
[music] But the glass has imperfections,
so a tiny little bit of light always
scatters back toward the source, [music]
kind of like a unique fingerprint. And
when a thunderquake happens, it vibrates
the glass, changing the fingerprint. So
by measuring lots of thunderquake
ripples with internet cables, we can
x-ray the ground. And they're trying to
use this idea to see below the surface
of other planets. To see it, subscribe.
